name: Agent harnesses
summary: The program wrapped around a model that turns it into an agent: it runs tools, asks permission, manages context and keeps memory.

D1.guide: Guess first: who actually runs the command, the model or the harness?
text: A model on its own can only write words. It cannot open files or press buttons.
A harness is the program around it. It reads what the model asks for, checks it is allowed, does it, and tells the model what happened.
D1.analogy: A learner driver in a dual-control car: the learner steers, the instructor can brake.

text: A **harness** is everything except the model: the loop that calls the model, the tools it is offered, the code that runs those tools, and the rules for what needs a person's approval. Examples include Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent.

It also manages **context**: what goes into each call (instructions, project notes, file contents, tool results) and what gets summarised or dropped as the window fills. Many harnesses plug in extra tools through a standard protocol such as MCP.
The same model can feel very different in different harnesses. Open harnesses let you choose the model, including one running on your own machine.

diagram.caption: What a harness wraps around the model

D2.analogy: A learner driver in a dual-control car.
D2.analogyBreaks: A learner improves with every lesson. A model learns nothing from a session unless the harness writes notes it can read next time, and the 'instructor' is a set of coded rules plus you approving actions.

predict.question: A harness lets the model run shell commands. Where is the safest place to enforce "never touch files outside this folder"?
options: In the system prompt, asked politely
In the harness's permission checks and sandbox, outside the model
predict.explanation: Instructions in the prompt can be ignored or overridden by injected text. Rules enforced by code outside the model hold whatever the model says.

text: Open problems: prompt injection, where text in a web page or file steers the agent, is unsolved, so harnesses lean on sandboxes and approvals. Constant approval prompts tempt people to allow everything.
Context management is still largely hand-tuned, and harnesses are hard to compare because results depend on the model, the tools and the task together.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents (Anthropic)
